title: atomic-prefill-window-merging-and-adaptive-kernel-probing-for-multi-stream-decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We observe intermittent CUDA graph capture failures and non-deterministic replay correctness when multiple decode streams compete and prefill windows align closely. Root cause appears to be small prefill boundary misalignment across streams causing kernel scheduling divergence and stale KV-cache pointers during graph replay. Goal: implement an atomic prefill-window merging layer that coalesces nearby prefill windows across streams and an adaptive kernel probing system that selects fallback kernels at capture-time to maximize replay stability without regressing tail latency. Deliverables: (1) prefill window coalescer algorithm integrated into scheduler, (2) a light-weight kernel probe shim that records per-model/per-seqlen winner kernels and fallback compatibility matrix, (3) a safety mode that forces single-stream capture for known-unsafe patterns, (4) unit/integration/regression tests and a canary rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Prefill coalescer merges adjacent prefill windows within configurable epsilon and reduces capture divergence events by >= 70% on internal stress suite
Adaptive kernel probe produces a compatibility matrix and reduces replay-time kernel fallbacks by >= 40% compared to baseline
End-to-end decode p99 latency regressed by no more than 5% on the 16k-token mixed workload
All new code covered by unit tests and CUDA-graph replay regression tests in CI
Canary rollout to 5% of traffic with automatic rollback if capture-failure rate > 0.5% or correctness checks fail
engineering_notes: Trade-offs: aggressive coalescing reduces capture churn but can increase per-request latency due to larger prefills; we add a tunable epsilon and per-tenant opt-out.
Kernel probing only runs at model load and when kernel library ABI/arch changes; results cached with TTL to avoid runtime overhead.
Implement compatibility matrix keyed by (model-shape, seqlen-bucket, device-arch) where entries point to preferred kernel id and safe fallbacks.
Decided against always forcing single-stream capture for long-prefill sequences (too high cost). Instead, add a conservative safety mode enabled only when probe indicates incompatibility.
Will reuse existing graph-capture tracing hooks from ENG-71234 to emit richer metadata (capture-id, kernel-ids, kv-pointer-checksum) needed for postmortem analysis.
test_plan: Unit: prefill coalescer function: boundary math, edge cases, tenant opt-out
Integration: isolated multi-stream harness that drives interleaved prefill patterns across 8 streams and asserts capture stability
Regression: add captured-replay-sanity test to CI that replays recorded captures on a separate node and validates output equality
Performance: run mixed workload (64/512/2048/16k tokens) comparing baseline runtime-2.3 vs runtime-2.4 pipeline, capture-failure and p99 latency measured
Chaos: induce kernel eviction and prefill misalignment in staging to ensure graceful fallback and no silent correctness regressions
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Merge feature branch behind feature flag and run extended nightly on staging for 72h
Stage 2: Canary 1% traffic, monitor capture-failure-rate, output-consistency checks, and p99 latency (2x sampling cadence)
Stage 3: Canary 5% traffic with automatic rollback thresholds (capture-failure > 0.5% or output-diff > 0.1% across sampled prompts)
Stage 4: Gradual ramp to 50% with DB of compatibility matrices shared across runtime fleet, then 100% if metrics stable for 48h
perf_results: Baseline staging run (runtime-2.3): intermittent capture divergence ~1.8% under interleaved-prefill stress harness, p99 decode latency 342ms on A100-40GB
Early prototype (coalescer + simple probe) measured capture divergence 0.46% on same harness and p99 latency 357ms (+4.4%)
With kernel-probing cache TTL tuned to 6h and conservative fallback enabled, replay fallbacks dropped 52% and capture divergence 0.34%
Next target: bring p99 regression <= +3% while keeping capture divergence < 0.5%
